sigma_analysis_results.rule_description:
Detects the execution of Xwizard tool from a non-default directory.
When executed from a non-default directory, this utility can be abused in order to side load a custom version of "xwizards.dll".

crowdsourced_ai_results.analysis: The analyzed binary is a legitimate Windows system component, specifically the 'Extensible Wizard Host' (xwizard.exe). The decompilation reveals standard Microsoft Active Template Library (ATL) code used for registry management (CRegParser, CRegKey) and COM object registration. The main execution flow involves parsing command-line arguments, loading the 'xwizards.dll' library, and managing activation contexts via Side-by-Side (SxS) assemblies. Relevant behaviors include window class registration ('Extensible Wizard Host') and event tracing via Event Tracing for Windows (ETW). There are no signs of malicious intent, obfuscation, or unauthorized persistence mechanisms.
